title: More Armstrong sides, and the gap before Ellington's first record
summary: He confirms If I Could Be with You belonged to the Armstrong sessions, then recalls weeks of theaters and dances before The Sheik was recorded the week after Easter 1932.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: On your recordings with Louis Armstrong you mentioned "I'm in the market for you", "Ding Dong Daddy", "Confessin'" and "Confession". And then I found a reference to "If I could be with you". Was that at the same time as the ones that you mentioned?
Yes. Yes. That was one of the same bunch that we made.

Getting back to your first days or weeks with Duke, the first date you played with Duke you said was at the Colonial Theater at Hartford, Connecticut where you played "Trees", and your first recording was the "Shiek of Araby" in New York. How much space of time was there between your first live appearance in the band and the first recording session?
Well, let's see. In those days we were playing these theaters week after week all the time. It was theaters one after another, and in between would be these

dance dates. And I don't remember too well how much time it was, but I know we were always doing something. And recording of this number "Shiek of Araby" was done in New York, I remember that much. And it wasn't too long after I had joined the band.
Do you think weeks, or months, or a couple of months, or --

Well, I'd have to look up in discography to find out the exact, you know, time between the numbers. Because as I said, we were always doing something. If it wasn't rehearsing, and we did a lot of club dates in which we carried a show -- a little floor show -- and we'd have to reherse for that. It's hard to remember any certain period.
Well, you -- you joined Duke out here in February, was that right?
Well, it was the week after Easter, I remember that, in 1932.
Oh, and -- well, according to the discography by Ashland, "Shiek of Araby" was recorded in May -- May 16, 1932.
It must have been recorded almost immediately.
Well, not too long. Of course, there was a little period I had to lay off.
